article.articleSummary:

- Philippines' Bureau of Animal Industry approves AVAC ASF LIVE, the first commercial vaccine against African swine fever (ASF) for fattening pigs, developed by AVAC Vietnam Joint Stock Company. The lyophilized, attenuated vaccine with inactivated genes is now permitted for public sale to help rebuild the country’s hog industry, which has suffered since ASF first struck in 2019, shrinking the national pig herd from about 13 million to around 8 million. A second vaccine, PROVAC from South Korea, is in BAI trials and could become available next year. ASF outbreaks have reached 76 of 82 provinces, with severe losses among small-scale producers lacking robust biosecurity and the capacity to absorb losses. article.articleHeadline: Qinghai Provincial Standing Committee of the People's Congress Conducts Enforcement Inspection of the Qinghai Province Echinococcosis Prevention and Control Regulation
article.articleSummary: From Aug 31 to Sep 3, 2026, the Qinghai Provincial Standing Committee of the People’s Congress conducted an enforcement inspection of the Qinghai Echinococcosis Prevention and Control Regulation in Yushu Prefecture. The team visited Zaduo and Chenduo counties, clinics, veterinary stations, schools, dog shelters, and villages to assess stray-dog control, wild-host surveillance, water-source protection, and echinococcosis screening, and gathered feedback from local officials and residents. They urged all levels to translate the regulation into action, refine task lists, and establish rectification logs, ensuring duties are carried out. Key measures include dog ownership registration, stray-dog cleanup, mandatory vaccination and comprehensive slaughter supervision for cattle and sheep, strengthening monitoring, and maintaining a grid-based information management system, patient management ledger, and routine home-visit medication guidance. The “Three Exemptions and One Subsidy” relief policy and cross-sector collaboration (health, agriculture, policing, forestry) were emphasized to prevent poverty and protect public health.

article.articleHeadline: Do you really need to wash your hair after getting drenched in the rain? Be careful not to contract a 'deadly disease'!
article.articleSummary: Two rain-related meningitis cases surfaced in China as of 2026-09-10. In Henan, a woman named Hai drenched for about 15 minutes developed convulsions, foaming at the mouth, and brief amnesia, later diagnosed with viral meningitis. In Changsha, Hunan, a 29-year-old man who was drenched after a night shift deteriorated overnight with fever, headache, vomiting, photophobia, and neck stiffness; he was diagnosed with purulent bacterial meningitis and moved to ICU. The report attributes risk to rain-induced immune suppression, allowing nasopharyngeal pathogens such as Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis to spread to the CNS. Early meningitis signs include fever, headache, fatigue, and vomiting; progression can be rapid, sometimes within 24 hours. Post-rain advice: wash hair and body with warm water and antiseptic, disinfect ears, and wash clothes separately after rain. Tianjin remains in a frequent rain period; seek care if fever or neck stiffness.

article.articleHeadline: Examining weather impacts on urban travel demand in Nanjing, China during the COVID-19 pandemic
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 pandemic in Nanjing, China, impacted public transport demand. Using February 2019–December 2022 monthly data, researchers analyzed weather–passenger flow relationships for buses, taxis, and Rail Transit System (RTS). Employing Random Forest (RF) and SHAP explanations, the study found RTS remained the dominant mode; overall passenger flow across all three modes fell sharply at the pandemic onset and gradually recovered. Temperature generally rose over the period; other weather variables varied. While RF and SHAP rankings were not fully aligned, both highlighted temperature and precipitation as influential factors shaping travel demand. A pandemic-driven modal shift occurred: pre-pandemic, mode shares were balanced; post-pandemic, taxi and RTS shares increased while bus ridership declined. Results offer a preliminary reference for adaptive urban transport planning under public-health disruptions and weather variability in Nanjing.

article.articleSummary: A 30-year-old woman from Shaanxi Province, China, presented with angular cheilitis misattributed to heat. The lesion expanded with high fever and weakness, then progressed to neurological symptoms and was diagnosed with herpes simplex encephalitis caused by HSV-1/HSV-2, leading to brain swelling and death. HSV-1 typically causes oral lesions and can reactivate when immunity wanes. Globally, HSV is a leading cause of fatal encephalitis; in the United States, about 10–20% of roughly 20,000 annual encephalitis cases are HSV-related, with untreated mortality up to 70%. Most HSV infections are mild, and CNS invasion is rare but rapidly progressive and often irreversible. Warning signs of CNS involvement include persistent fever, severe headache, vomiting, facial numbness or weakness, and altered consciousness—seek emergency care. Transmission is by contact during outbreaks; avoid kissing and sharing utensils. EBV is another herpesvirus discussed, classified as a carcinogen by WHO.

article.articleHeadline: Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences Netesov: ticks infected with the ALTNV virus are in Russia.
article.articleSummary: ALTVN is a newly identified virus from China; when co-infected with another pathogen it may lead to fatal outcomes. In Russia, this pathogen is not present, according to Sergey Netesov, head of the laboratory of bio-nanotechnology, microbiology and virology. Transmission occurs via tick bites; symptoms include high fever, gastrointestinal disturbance, and weakness. The virus is linked to the previously found Dabi virus and an unknown disease they reportedly co-operate with, though Russian researchers collected several dozen ticks and found no Dabi. The ticks carrying ALTVN appear limited to Primorsky Krai and possibly Khabarovsk Krai. Mortality is about 20% of patients, and there is no approved treatment as the pathogen remains under study. Daily Mail cites over 320 infections. In NEJM, ALTVN-only infections fully recovered, whereas co-infection with the tick virus DBV caused lung and kidney complications and fatalities.

article.articleHeadline: Dual RNA-seq Reveals Parasite Virulence Genes and Crab Immune Responses
article.articleSummary: On China's eastern coast, the swimming crab Portunus trituberculatus faces invasion by Mesanophrys sp., a scuticociliate parasite that colonizes hemolymph and destroys hemocytes, threatening farm populations. Ningbo University researchers report in Acta Parasitologica a dual RNA-seq study of in vitro Mesanophrys–hemocyte co-cultures, the first dual transcriptome of this interaction. In samples at 18 and 72 hours, crab hemocytes activate innate immunity via Toll-like receptor signaling, adaptor molecules, and MAPK pathways, with broad stress responses and metabolic shifts, yet damage proceeds. Mesanophrys shows enrichment of secreted proteases, including cysteine proteases, thimet oligopeptidase 1, and oligopeptidase B-like proteases, many with signal peptides indicating secretion. Gelatin zymography and protease inhibition confirm active enzymes. The work leverages Portunus trituberculatus genome (2020) to link extracellular proteases to hemocyte destruction, highlighting virulence mechanisms behind aquaculture losses in eastern China.

article.articleHeadline: Anthropic warns that someone is using AI to develop weapons and biological viruses
article.articleSummary: As of Sep 10, 2026, Anthropic published a 150-page intelligence report warning that generative AI has entered real-world use in hacking, surveillance, weapons development, and bioscience, with repeated references to China-linked actors. The report details attempts to bypass geolocation barriers via fake or stolen accounts, VPNs, and intermediaries to use Claude for attacks, monitoring, and risky biology research. China-related activity includes a CCP unit using Claude to scan social media for political sensitivities and to target individuals; a religion intelligence operation (GTG-14020) that uses AI to generate thousands of reports from sources on religious groups. The report cautions that AI lowers the barrier to surveillance, weapon design, and bioresearch across available tools. Other cases involve Mali, Iran, Yemen and Russia; five gain-of-function work on mosquito-borne virus. Seven Chinese labs conducted model distillation attacks (Alibaba, Moonshot, DeepSeek, Zhipu AI, SenseTime, MiniMax). Actions: accounts banned and authorities notified.

article.articleHeadline: Opinion | How the melting glaciers are unlocking ancient superbugs we've never seen before
article.articleSummary: Glacial melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) and adjacent regions is releasing ancient pathogens into modern watersheds. Notable events include the 2016 anthrax outbreak on Russia’s Yamal Peninsula—over 2,300 reindeer killed, dozens of people infected, one fatally—linked to thawed permafrost; recent Nepal floods (Bhotekoshi, Aug 26) and a July 2025 transboundary glacial flood triggered in China’s Gyirong County, which destroyed infrastructure and claimed several lives. Scientific work from the Tibetan Plateau (Guliya ice cap) recovered viral genomes up to 15,000 years old, later extended to 41,000 years with about 1,700 viral species, indicating ancient viral diversity; pathogens including Cryptococcus, Aureobasidium melanogenum, Naganishia albida, and Rhodotorula mucilosa were found in Greenland/Svalbard glaciers. A 30,000-year-old Siberian permafrost yielded a vancomycin-resistance gene, showing long-standing antibiotic resistance potential. The piece calls for proactive metagenomic surveillance, eDNA metabarcoding, and One Health-oriented expansion of sequencing to monitor glacier-fed systems and mitigate risks.

article.articleHeadline: CSL Seqirus Publishes Phase 3 Study Results for Influenza Vaccine
article.articleSummary: CSL Limited, an Australia-based biotech company, published Phase 3 results for an influenza vaccine through its CSL Seqirus segment, which specializes in influenza vaccines and pandemic services to governments. Its product lineup includes Respreeza, Zemaira, HAEGARDA, KCENTRA, Hepatitis B, Evogam, among others. The article notes Seqirus' focus on influenza-related products and pandemic preparedness. article.articleHeadline: International Leprosy Prevention and Control Training Course Arrives in Shandong, Sharing China's Leprosy Prevention and Control Experience.
article.articleSummary: On September 9, 2026, the Development Countries Leprosy Prevention and Control Technical Training Course conducted on-site teaching at Shandong First Medical University Affiliated Skin Disease Hospital (Shandong Institute of Leprosy Prevention and Control/Shandong Provincial Skin Hospital). Hospital president Zhang Furen outlined its 1955 origin as the Leprosy Research Institute and its evolution into a public-health–oriented, tertiary dermatology hospital with annual outpatient visits over 500,000. Guest speaker Dr. Lucinda Claire Fuller (Chelsea and Westminster Hospital; ILDS president) joined local experts Bo Fangfang and Wang Na, covering leprosy and skin NTDs, with hands-on lab and clinical demonstrations and tours of departments including traditional Chinese medicine dermatology and cosmetic laser clinics. Attendees also visited Shandong University, Jinan campus, and the Jinan Leprosy Ward. China aims to eliminate leprosy by 2030, has trained 67 professionals since 2019, and reports zero incidence/mortality of dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome.

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: Ebola Fatigue? the Anglican Church in DR Congo Launches New Phase of Response to the Ongoing Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: DRC's 17th Ebola outbreak, declared May 15, 2026 in the Democratic Republic of Congo, was designated a Public Health Emergency of International Concern within 48 hours by WHO. As of September 10, 2026, Ebola remains active in the eastern provinces of Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu and Haut-Uélé, with transmission fueled by high mobility, mining and cross-border movement amid ongoing conflict and displacement. Healthcare workers have suffered more than 40 deaths since the outbreak began. In response, six Anglican dioceses—Boga, Aru, Beni, Butembo, Kisangani and Kinshasa—launch a three-month capacity-building phase starting in September to strengthen community knowledge on transmission and prevention, promote hygiene in parish and community buildings, and train about 300 more community leaders and volunteers. Diocese of Aru led a workshop for religious and community leaders; the Anglican Health and Community Network supports knowledge sharing across affected areas.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Haut-Uele and Ituri assess the response to the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Sept 9–10, 2026, Ebola response in the cross-border region between Haut-Uele and Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo, was evaluated in Niania, Bandaka chiefdom, Mambasa territory. The joint mission of Ituri Military Governor General Kasongo Mulumba and Haut-Uele Vice-Governor Christophe Dara Matata aimed to assess field actions and strengthen collaboration as part of monitoring the evolution of the outbreak. The Bandaka chiefdom welcomed the authorities, underscoring the community’s need for clear signals amid Ebola concerns. The officials urged residents to cooperate with response teams and to bolster community surveillance to reduce transmission between the two provinces. Matata highlighted ongoing cross-provincial cooperation; Mulumba urged deeper community involvement. "Victory over Ebola is certain. It will end only if we collaborate well with health authorities." They reaffirmed commitments to support health teams and intensify sensitization in the border zone to curb spread.

article.articleHeadline: The mysterious last hours of a driver reveal the Democratic Republic of the Congo's deep fears in the face of Ebola.
article.articleSummary: In Ituri province, Marabo village, Democratic Republic of the Congo, a truck driver named Taylor Okito, 34, from Goma, was found dead after vomiting blood beside his idle truck on the Bunia–Kisangani route. Ebola remains the Congo’s most severe outbreak to date, with more than 3,000 deaths. Emergency responders formed a rapid team, collected a saliva sample, and moved the body, amid a village dispute over burial. A hospital test for Ebola returned negative, triggering concerns about false negatives and the need to trace contacts; the corpse remained in the responders’ truck for over an hour while relatives argued. Bundibugyo virus, the strain involved, is rare and requires specific testing; WHO has distributed rapid kits to enable on-site results. Authorities emphasize respectful handling and family consent to sustain outbreak response.

article.articleHeadline: 74 cases and eight deaths linked to monkeypox recorded in Luebo, in Kasai.
article.articleSummary: Monkeypox outbreak persists in Luebo health zone, Kasai province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Since the 35th epidemiological week, 74 cases and eight deaths have been recorded, per the Ministry of Public Health on September 10. Six of the zone’s 26 health areas are affected. The ministry is intensifying response measures to limit transmission and ensure care for affected individuals. A batch of medicines and other response resources has been dispatched to Luebo to strengthen case management. Rapid response teams will be deployed to assist provincial efforts, particularly in surveillance and patient management. Vaccination is being considered, with plans to evaluate vaccines used in previous response operations. Enhanced epidemiological surveillance will cover Kasai and other provinces to rapidly detect new cases.

article.articleHeadline: Climate change is shifting malaria hot spots in Africa
article.articleSummary: Malaria is shifting across Africa as climate change alters mosquito and parasite viability. A Nature study using century-long sub-Saharan blood samples links childhood malaria prevalence to temperature and precipitation, comparing a climate-change scenario with a no-change baseline. From 1901 to 2014, climate change likely caused a net 0.5% increase in transmission across sub-Saharan Africa—about one excess case per 1,000 children—with larger gains in eastern and southern Africa. In the Ethiopian highlands, transmission rose by 8 per 1,000 children; in parts of West Africa, rates fell by 1–2% (≈4 fewer per 1,000). Historically, West and Central Africa, including Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo, were hotbeds. Transmission peaks around 25°C and drops below 19°C or above 34°C. Looking ahead, climate change could lower regional transmission by ~2% over the next 85 years under a 2.7°C warming, though malaria control measures remain decisive.

article.articleHeadline: Experts want local medics to manage Laikipia Ebola facility
article.articleSummary: Kenyan experts at the Bioethics Society of Kenya conference in Nairobi urged Kenyan medics to manage the Laikipia Ebola containment facility, arguing local oversight would improve accountability and ensure Kenyan benefits. The facility, designed to isolate Americans exposed to Ebola while working in the region, is currently run by Americans; Kenya has not reported an Ebola case. Debates centered on governance, transparency, and who bears responsibility if negligence occurs or Kenyan citizens are exposed, with questions about whether the site could be treated as a sovereign US enclave. Health ethicists emphasized the risk to frontline workers, and the ethical use of experimental Ebola vaccines. The WHO notes no licensed vaccines or therapeutics for the Bundibugyo Ebola variant currently, spreading in DR Congo, while urging protection for health workers. The discussion linked bioethics to outbreak preparedness and human–wildlife interfaces.

article.articleHeadline: Five Additional H5 Bird Flu Events In NSW |
article.articleSummary: On 11 September 2026, New South Wales reports five new H5 bird flu events in Dee Why (Greater Crested Tern), Goulburn (Greater Crested Tern), Hawks Nest (Greater Crested Tern), Congo (White fronted tern), and Moruya (Silver Gull). NSW totals rise to 30 events, Australia 509. Dee Why marks the second Sydney metropolitan event after Warriewood earlier this month. The NSW Government is working with the poultry industry to reduce the virus risk. Bird flu has not been detected in commercial poultry flocks or captive birds, and the risk to human health remains low. The NSW Chief Veterinary Officer advises housing poultry where possible; further housing actions will follow risk assessment. No signs of mass mortality; ongoing surveillance and a national plan to monitor detections and enable rapid response. If you see sick or dead wildlife with H5 bird flu, avoid contact, record observations, and report online.

article.articleHeadline: Doctor flies to the Ebola region: "I rarely laugh as much as I do on missions."
article.articleSummary: Simone Hartel, a pediatric oncologist at Karlsruhe's municipal hospital, will depart for Ebola work in Bunia, in the northeast Democratic Republic of Congo. She will assume a leadership role at an Ebola Treatment Center, caring for infected patients and evaluating those with suspected infections to trace contacts and curb further spread. The deployment spans several weeks, supported by her team who covers her hospital duties back home. The northeast DRC outbreak is severe, with the WHO warning it could become Africa's worst Ebola surge, and at least 3,000 deaths reported in the region. There is no approved vaccine for the circulating strain. Common symptoms include high fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea; severe cases can cause kidney or liver failure. Hartel has previously worked in crisis zones with NGOs, including Ukraine, Myanmar, and Sudan, driven by vocation and faith.

article.articleHeadline: Haut-Uele: Kibali Gold Mine provides material support to the Ebola response.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Haut-Uele, Democratic Republic of the Congo, receives material support from Kibali Gold Mine. The company supplied response teams with 51,000 face masks, 51,000 pairs of medical gloves, 500 safety goggles, 100 thermoflash devices, two Toyota Land Cruiser ambulances, a Toyota hearse, 28 solar-powered street lights, 13 four-by-four meter tents, and 13 planks and tarps for shelters, plus additional protective gear and checkpoint kits. Governor Jean Bakomito Gambu praised the contribution as a major boost to the authorities’ Ebola response efforts. In Durba, Kibali had already built an Ebola Treatment Center and provided a laboratory to response teams. Tim Richard, Kibali’s operations director, emphasized health of populations as a priority and noted prior initiatives to strengthen prevention and local response. Kibali has operated in Haut-Uele for over sixteen years, underscoring the mining operator’s social and health involvement in the province.

article.articleHeadline: Cases of malaria in Alta Floresta raise alarm over transmission in MT.
article.articleSummary: Five malaria cases in Alta Floresta (Alto Tapajós), Mato Grosso, raise transmission risk in the northern state and Amazonia Legal. Mato Grosso has 1,154 malaria notifications in 2026, up from 986 in all of 2025 (17% higher). Other at-risk MT municipalities include Aripuanã, Colniza, Apiacás, Juruena, and Peixoto de Azevedo. Malaria remains endemic in the Amazon region, which accounts for about 99% of Brazil's cases; this year Brazil totals 65,887, with 63,585 in the Amazon. Amazonas leads with 30,875; Pará 13,650; Roraima 7,015; Rondônia 5,326. Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes; symptoms include fever, chills, sweats, headaches, body aches, weakness, nausea, and sometimes vomiting. Prevention emphasizes reducing bites—repellents, long sleeves, bed nets, screened openings—especially near rivers or floating structures; prompt care upon symptoms helps interrupt transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Chikungunya Cases in US Travelers Reach 89 with No Local Spread as Six Countries Carry Outbreak Notices
article.articleSummary: 89 travel-associated chikungunya cases diagnosed in US states through Aug 11, plus one in a US territory, with zero locally acquired cases, indicating no domestic transmission in 2026. Since 2015, travel-associated counts have varied (2020: 33; 2023: 152; 2024: 241; 2025: 628); current figures are preliminary due to reporting lags. Active outbreak notices cover Bolivia (Santa Cruz and Cochabamba), northwest Costa Rica, French Guiana, Mauritius, Nicaragua, and Suriname; ten countries pose elevated exposure for US travelers: Brazil, Colombia, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Peru, the Philippines, and Thailand. Florida’s week-ending Aug 29 report shows 55 travel-associated cases with onset this year; Miami-Dade accounted for 29, Hillsborough 8; about 40 cases originated in Cuba, with Nicaragua contributing eight; locally acquired chikungunya remains zero, while 73 locally acquired dengue occurred in five counties. Symptoms include fever and severe joint pain; there is no antiviral treatment, with diagnosis relying on travel history and supportive care, and fever within two weeks of return warrants medical evaluation.

Information about the breach was published on September 8. Teivida’s commercial director stated strict adherence to good hygiene practices, proper sanitation of equipment, and validated thermal processing; documents and veterinary permits were in order, and the chicken raised no suspicion. The lot was ordered as a substitute due to shortfalls from the regular supplier and was not stocked further or ordered again from that supplier. Salmonella bacteria can cause salmonellosis, presenting with diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever; higher risk for young children, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. No customer complaints were reported at that time.

article.articleHeadline: Nucleotide deletions in dengue virus 3' untranslated region compromises protein translation of live attenuated dengue vaccine strains - npj Vaccines
article.articleSummary: Brazil licensed TV003, a live attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine candidate, with DENV-1 and DENV-4 attenuated by 30-nucleotide deletions (Δ30) in the 3'UTR and a DENV-4 Δ30 backbone used to make a DENV-2 prM/E chimera. DENV-3 attenuation requires an additional Δ30/31 in the 3'UTR. In comparisons with wild-type Sleman/78 and a partially attenuated DENV-3 (Δ30), protein/RNA pulldown showed the 3'UTR binds host translation proteins, including ribosomal proteins, EIF3D, and EIF3K, promoting viral protein expression. Reduced binding of EIF3D/EIF3K to Δ30/31 coincides with lower genome translation and replication; silencing EIF3D similarly lowers protein expression and replication of Sleman/78 and Δ30. Silencing EIF4E had no significant effect. Δ30 attenuates DENV-1 and -4 but does not impair DENV-2 translation, potentially explaining reactogenicity. The study clarifies 3'UTR interactions and suggests updating vaccine components with more contemporaneous DENVs.

article.articleHeadline: Five mpox cases confirmed in Ceará in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) cases in Ceará, Brazil reach five confirmed in 2026, all men aged 20–45. Ceará logged 67 notifications this year, with 62 discarded. Nationally, Brazil reports 14,847 confirmed mpox cases, 141 probable, 128 suspected, and 18 deaths, per the Ministério da Saúde; São Paulo has 199 confirmations and Rio de Janeiro 112. Diagnosis uses molecular laboratory testing, preferably from lesion secretions; when lesions dry, scabs may be analyzed. The first Ceará confirmation in 2026 was on March 9, with a favorable outcome. Since 2022 Ceará maintains ongoing surveillance and case investigation. Preventive measures include avoiding close contact with suspected/confirmed cases, hand hygiene, and masking in risk settings. There is no specific mpox treatment; care is supportive. Mpox is a zoonotic Orthopoxvirus transmitted via contact with lesions, secretions, or contaminated items; incubation 3–21 days, with symptoms such as rash, fever, lymphadenopathy, and malaise; most recover in 2–4 weeks.

article.articleHeadline: Marataízes: Twelve active cases help understand the control of the chickenpox outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Marataízes, Brazil, reports 129 confirmed chickenpox (varicella) cases in the current outbreak, with 117 recoveries and 12 active cases in the latest epidemiological bulletin. Data cover roughly two months of follow-up; active cases offer a recent snapshot, while the total remains cumulative. A decline from peak daily probable cases suggests a favorable shift, though transmission may continue. Chickenpox causes vesicular skin lesions with fever, fatigue, and malaise, and spreads mainly via respiratory droplets and close contact, especially in crowded settings. Prevention centers on vaccination; residents should verify vaccination status and stay up to date. Additional measures include avoiding close contact with symptomatic individuals, monitoring for fever and lesions, seeking care for suspected cases, and following isolation where confirmed. Dr. Paulo Vinicius Cordeiro Novais, Coordinator of Epidemiological Surveillance, emphasizes vaccination as the main preventive measure.

article.articleHeadline: Paraná's animal neutering program also offers a rabies vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Paraná's permanent neutering program for dogs and cats (CastraPet Paraná) now includes rabies vaccination distribution, reinforcing zoonosis prevention and animal-human health protection in Paraná, Brazil. While classic canine rabies variants are controlled in Brazil, the virus remains circulating in the wild cycle, notably among bats. Various species can carry the virus and spread it through saliva, mainly via bites; scratches or contact with saliva on mucous membranes or broken skin are rarer routes. Cats warrant heightened attention due to predatory behavior and greater exposure to bats, potentially linking wild and urban transmission cycles. Per the Regional Council of Medicine of Paraná (CRM-PR), vaccination against rabies is essential and should be kept up to date, even in older animals. Bats are wild and legally protected under federal law 9605/98; if contact occurs, follow official guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Do slugs transmit disease? See when there is a risk.
article.articleSummary: Angiostrongylus cantonensis and A. costaricensis can infect humans, primarily through ingestion of infected mollusks or contaminated foods. A. cantonensis causes neural angiostrongyliasis with eosinophilic meningitis; A. costaricensis causes abdominal angiostrongyliasis. In Brazil, recent studies have found A. cantonensis in various terrestrial mollusks, including species in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. Slugs, snails, and other gastropods are not interchangeable; risk depends on the specific species. Exposure occurs mainly when a person unknowingly eats a small mollusk or foods contaminated by their parasites; mucus exposure is possible but not well proven. If a slug is found at home, avoid handling with bare hands; wear gloves or use a plastic bag, then wash hands. Clean surfaces and discard foods touched by the animal; reducing moisture and debris around the home lowers the risk. If neurological symptoms emerge after exposure, seek medical care and report contact.

Regions with elevated Aedes aegypti activity include East (Alto Taquaral, Parque Taquaral, Chácara Primavera), Northwest (Cidade Satélite Íris I), North (CDHU Edvaldo Orsi, Jardim Mirassol, Vila Renascença, Parque Maria Helena), Southwest (Vida Nova I/II, Mauro Marcondes, Jardim Santos Dumont II, Eldorado dos Carajás), South (Jardim São Domingos, Jardim Marisa, Vila Palmeiras I–II, Jardim Fernanda I–II), and Southeast (Jardim Esmeraldina, Jardim Samambaia, Jardim Tamoio, Jardim Aliança, Jardim Estoril). The alert also covers adjacent areas. From Jan 1 to Sep 8, 2026, 3,925 dengue cases were confirmed in Campinas. Health teams conducted over 1.2 million home visits and more than 53,000 backpack foggings. Indoor foci account for about 80% of breeding sites. Prevention emphasizes eliminating standing water; change water in plant pots every 2 days, clean saucers weekly, seal water tanks, and keep unused toilets closed. Community cooperation and identifiable workers are emphasized.

article.articleHeadline: The Dangers of Polio
article.articleSummary: Polio could re-emerge globally if international health authorities become complacent, epidemiological models warn. The last poliomyelitis case in Brazil occurred in Sousa, Paraíba, on 19 March 1989; the Americas were declared polio-free in 1994 thanks to vaccination. In 2023 there were 12 cases (six in Pakistan, six in Afghanistan); by end-July 2026, 18 cases had been diagnosed, with Pakistan and Afghanistan remaining endemic. Vaccination campaigns since 1988 have driven eradication, delivering about 1 billion doses to 400 million children annually. Over the last decade, about $3 billion was allocated to Afghanistan and Pakistan, but Covid-19 disruption, political instability, and conflicts diverted resources. In January 2026, the United States left the WHO, cutting roughly 30% of the Global Polio Eradication Initiative funding for 2026–27. The Gates Foundation pledged $1.2 billion (2026–2029); Rotary International, with about 1.2 million members, will raise $50 million per year for vaccination campaigns.

The application, using tractors and hoses, follows prior deployments at Parque Ecológico Municipal Zoo Americana, Córrego Bertini, Avenida Bandeirantes, and the shores of Namorados Beach and Blue Beach, as part of a city-wide effort in high-risk areas. The operation is conducted in partnership with the State Institute of Biological Control and Toyobo, with oversight by the Municipal Health Department. The PVCE program maintains warnings and barriers across risk zones along rivers and reservoirs, including Carioba fishing sites near the Piracicaba River and other riparian areas. Febre maculosa presents with high fever, body aches, chills, and a red rash; prevention includes light clothing, tucking pants into socks, regular tick checks, careful removal, and seeking prompt medical care after exposure.

article.articleHeadline: West Nile virus: cases spike in the country, leaving the population on alert
article.articleSummary: West Nile virus (WNV) cases surged in Italy through September 8, 2026, with 594 infections and 41 deaths reported by the ISS, including 306 neuroinvasive cases. The outbreak spans 79 provinces across 19 regions, marking a 14% rise from the previous bulletin (521 cases). The virus has also been detected in Brazil, with new cases appearing in August 2026. WNV is an arbovirus transmitted by Culex mosquitoes; birds are the natural reservoirs. Most infections are asymptomatic, but about 20% develop fever, body aches, headache, fatigue, nausea, or rash; a small proportion progress to neuroinvasive disease such as meningitis, encephalitis, or paralysis. Prevention focuses on reducing mosquito bites and breeding sites: repellents, protective clothing, screens, and avoiding litter in ditches and streams. At-risk groups include the elderly, immunosuppressed, and people with chronic diseases. Several vaccine candidates exist, but none licensed.

article.articleHeadline: The History of Ancol Reclamation: Former Wetlands That Were Malaria Breeding Grounds
article.articleSummary: Ancol, in North Jakarta, was historically marshland known as a malaria mosquito breeding ground. By the 1960s the area remained swampy and malaria-prone, prompting a shift toward tourism development. Dutch East Indies Governor Adriaan Valckenier first eyed Ancol for potential tourist development in the early 17th century, but realisation was delayed by priorities and independence-era conflicts. In December 1965, President Sukarno ordered and appointed Governor H. Soemarno Sosroatmodjo to lead the project. article.articleHeadline: Wang Yikang: ASEAN nations must unite to tackle three major epidemics.

With NCD burden rising due to higher living standards and aging populations, regional cooperation is needed, including nutrition labeling—adopted by Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Smoking and electronic cigarettes are key risk factors; some ASEAN members ban e-cigarettes, but cross-border flow persists, calling for a coordinated regional response. AMR is described as a 'silent pandemic'; actions include keeping antibiotics as prescription medicines and curbing illegal prescribing. For Disease X, vaccines remain essential; WHO, CEPI, and Gavi reinforce preparedness, and ASEAN should map vaccine needs, identify priority products, build production capacity, and bolster regulation via the ASEAN Center for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases.

article.articleHeadline: In critical condition after contracting Whitmore's disease
article.articleSummary: A 53-year-old man in Quang Ninh Province, Vietnam (Bai Chay Hospital) is diagnosed with melioidosis (Whitmore's disease) caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei after blood and sputum cultures. He presented with fever, rigors, productive cough and progressively worsening dyspnea, with CT showing right upper-lobe pneumonia, multiple nodules and bilateral hazy infiltrates, partial lower-lobe atelectasis, thickened interstitium and small right pleural effusion. He had severe infection with white blood cell count 24.5 x 10^9/L, neutrophils 89%, procalcitonin 14.53 ng/mL and hypoxemia (PaO2 54 mmHg, SpO2 91% on oxygen). Treated in ICU with mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, fluids, continuous renal replacement therapy and hemoperfusion. After two days, blood and sputum cultures were positive for Burkholderia pseudomallei, confirming Whitmore's disease; the patient gradually improved with declining infection markers and better respiratory function. Public health note: avoid self-medication and seek medical care for prolonged fever, cough, chest pain or signs of severe infection.

article.articleHeadline: Urticaria in children: Do not overlook infections and rash types that are easily mistaken.
article.articleSummary: Urticaria in children is not synonymous with allergy; viral infections are a common trigger for acute hives. Classic urticaria presents pink or red wheals that itch, appear quickly, and may spread, with each lesion usually resolving within 24 hours without scarring. If hives accompany lip or tongue swelling, vomiting, abdominal pain, wheezing, or breathing difficulty, systemic anaphylaxis must be considered and treated promptly. Recurrent hives with no clear food or medicine trigger, especially during fever, cough, runny nose, or diarrhea, should not be labeled as food allergy. Infections, particularly viruses, can cause hives; bacteria such as group A Streptococcus, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae may accompany rashes but do not justify antibiotics without confirmed infection. Distinguish fixed lesions lasting more than a day, painful or purplish with bleeding or bullae, from urticaria. Four warning signs: rapid onset with trigger, multisystem symptoms, fixed duration, and fever with purpura requiring urgent evaluation.

article.articleHeadline: Mycobacterium tuberculosis attacks a man's lungs and prostate.
article.articleSummary: 37-year-old Cambodian Anh Phongsay in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, presented with fever, productive cough, nausea and weight loss, diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis with prostatic involvement. MRI showed lung consolidation and numerous 1–2 mm nodules; biopsy and culture were acid-fast bacilli positive, indicating TB spreading from the lung to the prostate. He has systemic lupus erythematosus for over two years with renal, hematologic and joint involvement. Managed with standard anti-TB therapy, infection-control antibiotics, and corticosteroid adjustment for SLE, and isolated in a dedicated room. After one week, fever subsided, dyspnea resolved, appetite returned, suitable for discharge. TB bacteria can reach the prostate hematogenously or from other sites; progression can be insidious with non-specific symptoms. Lupus and immunosuppressive therapy increase TB risk; patients on immunosuppressants require regular follow-up and prompt evaluation for prolonged fever, cough, fatigue, weight loss, or night sweats.

She tested positive for influenza A and required endotracheal intubation with mechanical ventilation. After initial improvement and a one-day extubation, she developed bulbar weakness, poor cough, and reduced airway protection, necessitating reintubation and continued ventilation. Neurophysiological testing and positive anti-AChR antibodies confirmed myasthenia gravis. She underwent four plasmapheresis sessions, corticosteroids, pyridostigmine, and respiratory support. Roughly 10 days later, her condition improved significantly; by day 24 she was alert, breathing spontaneously, coughing effectively, and discharged. This case highlights that myasthenia gravis can be triggered or unmasked by infection and cause severe respiratory failure requiring ventilatory support.

article.articleHeadline: Ludhiana: Dengue larvae detections drop amid weak monsoon

District epidemiologist Dr. Supreet Kaur attributes the drop in larval detections to less rainfall, though dengue cases remain unchanged: 36 dengue-positive cases reported so far this year, matching the count on the same date last year. She cautions that a higher later-year tally is possible; only 36 cases were reported by September 8 last year, but infections spiked in October–November, yielding 539 cases by December. She blames a week-long sanitation workers’ strike in late July for creating breeding conditions despite reduced rainfall, as garbage accumulation hindered street cleaning.

India's institutional deliveries rose from 78% to 93%, contributing to declines in maternal and child mortality. Tedros also highlighted India's End TB efforts, strengthened regulation of medical products, support to WHO on traditional medicine, and ongoing Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing discussions under the WHO Pandemic Agreement, ahead of the 79th Regional Committee meeting.

article.articleHeadline: Even after spending thousands of crores, the mosquito menace has not diminished; dengue fears persist.
article.articleSummary: Dengue remains a major public health issue in Dhaka, even after extensive spending on vector control. From Jan 1 to Sep 9, 2026, the country logged 133 dengue deaths, with 63 of them in Dhaka’s two city corporations (DNCC and DSCC). National hospitalizations reached 46,938, including 12,822 in Dhaka. In 2023, hospitalizations were 321,179 with 1,705 deaths nationwide. For vector control, DNCC allocated 688 crore 39 lakh taka and DSCC 323 crore 63 lakh taka across 2023–24 to 2025–26; in 2025–26, DNCC budgeted 187 crore 75 lakh and DSCC 53 crore 50 lakh. Despite fogging and larviciding, residents report only temporary relief. Public-health expert Dr Wahid Jaman says Dhaka has never relied on a scientific eradication approach, and calls for integrated measures—breeding-site destruction and community engagement—similar to Kolkata. Officials could not be reached for comment.

article.articleHeadline: Exclusive: Ghaziabad company blacklisted over polio now stopped from making rabies vaccine
article.articleSummary: CDSCO has prohibited Ghaziabad-based Bio Med from manufacturing anti-rabies vaccines for humans after BET failures in several batches of its Sure Rab vaccine. Two batches, R030126 and R011125, were Not of Standard Quality, with one batch also failing bovine serum albumin limits; a stop-production order followed a joint inspection with the UP FDA. Bio Med, founded in 2002, is among five Indian anti-rabies vaccine manufacturers, alongside Indian Immunologicals Limited, Bharat Biotech, Serum Institute of India and Cadila. The action follows a separate probe into a suspected counterfeit Abhayrab batch linked to a Delhi premises. Bio Med was previously blacklisted from supplying polio vaccines since 2018 due to type-2 poliovirus contamination in OPV. India bears a high rabies burden: about 58 lakh animal-bite cases annually (≈47 lakh dog bites) and over 5,700 deaths. Government says no current vaccine shortage; quality lapses raise public-health concerns.

article.articleHeadline: EMPE Diagnostics to Unveil CircuLOK Product Range at NATCON 2026, Expanding Access to TB Drug-Resistance Diagnostics - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: EMPE Diagnostics AB unveils CircuLOK TB drug-resistance testing at NATCON 2026 in Patiala, India (Oct 1–4), expanding its modular TB molecular resistance portfolio for laboratories to tailor coverage and scale testing. CircuLOK MDR-TB detects rifampicin and isoniazid resistance; CircuLOK pre-XDR-TB adds fluoroquinolone resistance alongside rifampicin/isoniazid; CircuLOK FLQ-TB provides standalone fluoroquinolone reflex testing. Together, the tests offer a spectrum from targeted FQ reflex to broader MDR and pre-XDR coverage across diagnostic networks. CircuLOK will be introduced for Research Use Only (RUO) at NATCON while EMPE pursues CDSCO approval and ICMR evaluation, following the same Indian regulatory pathway as existing TB diagnostics. Produced at EMPE’s ISO 13485 facility in Hyderabad under Make in India, which also hosts R&D and validation, the firm aims to extend resistance coverage toward the WHO-recommended BPaLM regimen from a single platform, per CEO Jan Buch Andersen.

article.articleHeadline: "Just as people can lie, so can governments": According to a study, the COVID-19 death toll was much higher.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 mortality underreporting: An Israeli study analyzing data from 134 countries/territories found official COVID-19 deaths (2020–2021) totaled 5.08 million, while estimated deaths due to the pandemic were about 12.47 million, implying that 45–55% of governments underreported deaths, with undercounting more common than overcounting. The study argues governance quality and institutional checks, plus citizens’ ability to scrutinize information (education, internet access), partly explain accuracy beyond data collection capacity. Notable examples include Chile, where data were relatively accurate due to stronger institutional constraints, versus Russia with substantial undercounting. India showed the largest absolute gap (official ~0.5 million vs ~4.5 million excess deaths); Nicaragua reported official deaths <250 versus thousands in excess mortality. Belarus and Egypt had limited testing despite high infections. The authors caution that gaps arise from testing and death-registration flaws and advocate using multiple sources when official data are questionable. Date: 2026-09-10.

article.articleHeadline: Dhaka meat market: Unsafe slaughter, weak checks expose health risks
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis killed 48-year-old Ajit Sarkar in Dhaka after fever and dangerously low platelets, underscoring health risks from unsafe slaughter and weak checks. The case aligns with Bangladesh’s longstanding link between animal handling and infection. Last year, northern Bangladesh saw anthrax outbreaks tied to cattle and meat processing, with 16 confirmed cases (media tallies up to 25), including 17 in Rangpur and eight in Gaibandha. Open slaughter, inadequate pre-slaughter health screening, and sparse veterinary oversight endanger consumers, livestock handlers, meat sellers. The Animal Slaughter and Meat Quality Control Act prohibits open slaughter except during family/religious events and requires veterinary examination with official carcass seals, yet seals are rarely found. Two modern slaughterhouses in Hazaribagh and Kaptanbazar (Tk81 crore) sit idle; capacity 30 cattle and 60 goats per hour, with plans to lease or privatize. Dhaka still experiences market-based slaughter in lanes and shops.

Ventilators exist in Kapoorthala and Gurdaspur Civil Hospitals but lack trained staff; Amritsar has 4 of 20 ventilators functional. Temiflu stocks are sufficient in government hospitals. Symptoms include fever, sore throat, cough, and fatigue; diagnosis can be negative early. Preventive measures: hygiene, masks, social distancing, vaccination, fluids.

article.articleHeadline: A flood in Nepal washed ashore unknown fish weighing 45 kg. Whoever ate them fell ill.
article.articleSummary: On Aug 26, 2026, an ice–rock avalanche in Nepal’s Rasuwa district released floodwaters that flowed via Lhende Khola into Bhote Koshi and down the Gandaki river system toward Bihar, India. In the Gandaki plains, fishermen reported giant fish—27, 38, 40 and 45 kg, with other sightings up to 50 kg—along with similar finds in West Champaran and Valmikinagar, Bihar. Bihar’s Department of Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources advised against catching, selling, or eating these fish due to contamination risk. Authorities as of Sept 9, 2026 still listed the specimens as unidentified. Samir Kumar Sinha (Wildlife Trust of India) preliminarily linked the fish to Bagarius bagarius (goonch catfish), and FishBase notes possible lengths up to 230 cm; an Oxford Academic study indicates Bagarius has largely vanished from some bihari river sections since 2014. Reported symptoms after consumption include vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dizziness, and breathing difficulties; the exact disease mechanism remained unconfirmed. Official case counts were not disclosed.

The advisory, issued September 8, emphasizes coverage for medical and other emergencies. For emergencies in Vietnam, Filipinos can contact +84 904 126 164 via SMS/WhatsApp/Viber/Zalo or email hanoipe.atn@dfa.gov.ph. The guidance aims to mitigate travel-associated health risks as tourism continues.

article.articleHeadline: Lancet Publication Marks Important Advance in Influenza Prevention for Older Adults | Taiwan News | Sep. 11, 2026 06:51
article.articleSummary: Phase 3 study results for MF59-adjuvanted cell-based higher-dose quadrivalent influenza vaccine (aQIVc), marketed as AUJEMFLU, were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, following MHRA approval for adults 50+ and EC approval for the same group. The multicountry immunogenicity trial enrolled 7,699 adults aged 50+ across Canada, Denmark, Estonia, Germany, Pakistan, the Philippines, the United Kingdom and the United States, comparing aQIVc with MF59-adjuvanted egg-based quadrivalent and recombinant quadrivalent vaccines. Primary outcomes showed superiority versus the egg-based vaccine across all four strains and age groups; non-inferiority versus recombinant for three strains in 50+ and all four strains in 65+; immune responses sustained through the influenza season; safety well tolerated with mostly mild/moderate reactions resolving within three days. Exploratory neuraminidase antibody enhancements observed. Regulatory submissions for a trivalent formulation are underway with phased introductions planned.

article.articleHeadline: Checklist Unveiled: 4 Infectious Disease Groups, Silent Threats of the Rainy Season
article.articleSummary: Thailand's rainy season raises infection risk. Nawavej Hospital highlights eight priority diseases and practical self-care, noting damp environments amplify spread of viruses, bacteria, and mosquitoes. Influenza presents with abrupt high fever, chills, headache, body aches, cough, and sore throat; prevention: yearly flu vaccine, masks, and hand hygiene. Pneumonia features fever with productive cough and shortness of breath; prevention: vaccination (especially for the elderly and chronically ill), masks, and hygiene. Diarrhea includes fever, nausea/vomiting, cramps, and watery stools; prevent with safe water (boiled/bottled), freshly cooked foods, avoiding raw or fly-tainted items, and thorough reheating. Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease mainly affects children under 5, with fever followed by mouth/hand/foot lesions; prevention: vaccines for circulating strains and regular handwashing. Leptospirosis—zoonotic from water/mud exposure—causes fever and calf pain; prevent by avoiding barefoot wading and wearing boots/gloves in flooded areas. Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika are mosquito-borne; dengue can cause shock/bleeding, chikungunya joint pain, Zika milder symptoms—eliminate standing water and use repellents, especially for pregnant women. Seek prompt medical care for persistent fever or breathing difficulties.

article.articleHeadline: The fungus capable of transforming insects into hosts and altering their behavior before it grows out of the body.
article.articleSummary: Zombie fungus Ophiocordyceps unilateralis complex infects Camponotus carpenter ants in tropical forests, with Thailand studies documenting the behavior-altering sequence. Spores contact the ant, penetrate the cuticle, and fungal growth yields profound physiological changes, culminating in a 'death grip' where the ant bites vegetation and dies, enabling fungal reproduction. A peduncle emerges from the head or body to release spores and disperse them. Brain invasion is not strictly required; research shows mandibular muscle hypercontraction and selective neuronal preservation, indicating a complex neuromuscular manipulation rather than simple brain takeover. After the host dies, the cadaver supports the reproductive structure and spore production; location matters for transmission, as nest-locus deaths may be removed by workers, while cadavers on vegetation promote spread. Fossil evidence suggests this interaction dates to ~48 million years ago, making the fungus a key model for evolution and host-pathogen dynamics.

article.articleHeadline: Infectious-disease specialist Zhemchugov explained the COVID-19 outbreak in Phuket.
article.articleSummary: New Phuket COVID-19 outbreak affects Russian tourists and relocants, with travelers reporting heavy symptoms and several days spent in bed. Virologist Vladislav Zhemchugov explains that newly emerged strains often cause milder disease since the virus benefits from not killing its human carriers, though severe courses remain possible. He notes that mutation is random and that a strain may interact with influenza or a local febrile infection; early symptoms across viral diseases are similar, including fever, headache, and muscle pain. The eventual severity depends on the virus's properties and the patient's health status, with pre-existing heart or lung disease increasing respiratory involvement and diabetes worsening outcomes for COVID-19. Studying the structure of the new strain is essential to understand its differences from previous variants. The article emphasizes the time needed to uncover these changes.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : Suspected Anthrax Recorded In Muchinga Province
article.articleSummary: Zambia reports suspected anthrax in Muchinga Province’s Mpika, Lavushimanda and Shiwang’andu districts. About 40 animals have died and 11 people are suspected to be affected. The government has launched assessments through Provincial and District Disaster Risk Management structures to determine outbreak extent and coordinate containment. The National Disaster Risk Management Division (DRMD) and the National Disaster Technical Committee of Permanent Secretaries met on September 8, 2026, to review the reports and advise actions. Environmental pollution has been reported in the affected areas. Public guidance urges residents not to consume, sell, or handle meat from animals that died suddenly or are suspected to have died from anthrax; avoid handling wild animals; avoid contact with blood or tissues from suspected animals; and promptly report unusual animal deaths to veterinary, health, or disaster management authorities. Authorities will continue monitoring and coordinating interventions; the public should remain calm and follow official guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Human and dog toxocariasis in Ghana revealed by molecular and serological
article.articleSummary: In Ghana’s Ashanti and Bono East regions, a surveillance study (January–October 2025) screened 505 people and 442 dogs, revealing human anti-Toxocara IgG seroprevalence of 14.5% overall (95% CI 11.4–17.5). Among children aged 6–15, seropositivity was 23.9%; ages 16–30, 4.5%; males 18.6%; rural residents 27.5%. Canines showed infection in 56.1% of dogs; of positives, 87.9% were Toxocara canis and 12.1% T. cati—the first molecular confirmation of T. cati in Ghanaian dogs. Toxocariasis arises from embryonated eggs shed by dogs and cats, with human infection via contaminated soil, water, vegetables, or fur, causing visceral or ocular larva migrans and related symptoms. Serology used NovaTec Toxocara IgG ELISA; cross-reactivity with Ascaris lumbricoides cannot be excluded; no confirmatory Western blot performed. Findings signal notable zoonotic exposure in settings with limited sanitation and veterinary care.
